The transcript rejects an 'Introducing…' title and suggests 'Why we scale on queue depth, not CPU: Riverbend Autoscaling 2.0', which puts the engineering claim ahead of the product name. The 'backlog that CPU can't see' section states the problem in general terms any engineer would recognize: I/O-bound workers keep CPU low while the queue grows. But the draft's first sentence opens with the product: '**Autoscaling 2.0 adds workers when work is waiting…**'.
